Select 1×, 2× or 4× Z width below the view. Each selection loads its own CAD and downloads. Z uses a full-depth NEMA17 with 40 mm travel, attached only through its base face. Z is inverted: motor above, output downward. The upright 1× NEMA14 radial actuator mounts directly through its threaded lid and retains 120 mm travel.

Output, base and lid mounts use the current 31 × 31 mm grid. The support uses recessed M3 screws into the Z base inserts; the direct radial lid has twelve printed M3×0.5 threads. The 2× output is 104 mm wide. Mounting coordinates · Mounting parts · STL

The compact radial actuator end is 147 mm from Z, 105 mm closer than before. Its motor sits 105 mm behind Z; the shorter body retains 120 mm travel. Pivots are 245 mm from board center on a 690 × 690 mm platform, preserving the short probe extension and 100 × 100 mm working area. The PCB surface is now 79.2 mm high, 204.8 mm lower. Z has 10 mm free clearance beyond its upper rear controller envelopes.

The Z support has two mirrored, staggered three-hole braces and matching 28 mm corner gussets, a flat outer print face and seven rounded relief windows. The middle deck mounts spread to X=±58 mm and the center mount moves to Y=64 mm. The taller STL is oriented face-down with a 206 × 324 mm footprint. The shared deck has nine open insert bores and twelve smaller cutouts. Its CAD volume is 16.2% below the unrelieved version.

Green translucent volumes reserve space for the rear controller components and USB cables. Component height, spacers and cables are provisional allowances. Load capacity, stiffness, contact force, print fit and accuracy remain untested. The checked module explosion separates one arm, withdraws the direct-lid screws into access wells, and separates the actuator modules. Actuator drives stay assembled; switch to Four arms for coordinated probing.

Based on FLEX, compliant-spur-gear, and the RP2040 motor controller.
